profile.reading: Per QTS own site, RIC3 DC3 is located at 3535 Portugee Road, Sandston, VA 23150 on the QTS Richmond 3 campus, a 221 acre master-planned campus with 240 MW planned upon completion across five Freedom Design buildings (DC1-DC5). Individual building square footage and phased MW capacity are not published.

profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021, at $78/share. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Richmond, Virginia mega-campus, spanning Henrico County and Sandston. This is QTS's flagship facility story: in 2010 QTS converted a former semiconductor manufacturing site into what Wikipedia describes as a 1.3 million square foot mega data center.

reading.body:
QTS's Richmond 3 campus in Virginia represents a 221-acre master-planned facility designed for 240 MW total capacity across five buildings, though individual building specifications remain unpublished.

The conversion of a former semiconductor manufacturing site into data center infrastructure illustrates how real estate and power capacity constrain AI expansion. QTS was acquired by Blackstone for $10 billion in 2021, signaling how infrastructure operators have become strategic assets in the path from electricity to compute. The Richmond location matters because Virginia data centers depend on regional power grids, and planned capacity across five phased buildings suggests deployment tied to power availability rather than all at once.

This dataset does not specify which buildings are operational, their individual MW allocations, or timeline for the remaining construction. Per-building power delivery requirements and connection points to the regional grid are also absent. The sources attempted reveal a research limitation: direct operator sites either redirect or serve unrelated companies, making verification of current status difficult beyond the campus-level plan.
